texto: The clause is divided into two sentences:

filas: Case under the main clause (der / den / dem)

texto: The «wer» (nominal), «wen» (accusative) or «wem» (dative) pronoun is governed by its own subordinate. The main clause retakes that person with «der» (nominating), «den» (accusative) or «dem» (dative) according to the syntactic function that it performs in the main. For example: **Wer fleißig lernt, der besteht die Prüfung** (nominee in both); **Wem das Team vertraut, den wählt man zum Sprecher** («wem» in dative by vertrauen, «den» in indicative by wählen).

bloques.titulo: Act of the award of the citizen's prize

frases.de: Wer sich ehrenamtlich engagiert, der verdient den Respekt der ganzen Stadt.
frases.es: Quien se compromete de forma voluntaria, ese merece el respeto de toda la ciudad.
frases.en: Anyone who voluntarily commits himself deserves the respect of the whole city.
analisis: who is committed on a voluntary basis

frases.de: Das stimmt vollkommen. Und wer anderen hilft, dem sollte man auch Unterstützung bieten.
frases.es: Es completamente cierto. Y a quien ayuda a otros, a ese se le debería ofrecer también apoyo.
frases.en: It's completely true. And to whom he helps others, he should also be given support.

frases.de: Genau. Wer ein echtes Vorbild ist, der erhält heute diese besondere Auszeichnung.
frases.es: Exacto. Quien es un auténtico modelo a seguir, ese recibe hoy esta distinción especial.
frases.en: Exactly. Who is a true model to follow, this special distinction is received today.
analisis: who is a true model to follow

frases.de: Eine wunderbare Würdigung für engagierte Bürger.
frases.es: Un reconocimiento maravilloso para ciudadanos comprometidos.
frases.en: A wonderful recognition for committed citizens.

bloques.pregunta: What syntactic function does the «Wer …, der …» correlation play in a formal discourse?

opciones.texto: It establishes a general wording applicable to any person who meets the condition expressed in the first clause.
opciones.explicacion: It works as a relative universal generalizer for undetermined people.

opciones.texto: It limits the claim to an individual mentioned only with a previous name and surname.
opciones.explicacion: «Wer» does not require prior antecedent; it includes any hypothetical subject.

opciones.texto: It serves as an indirect style formula for citing witness statements.
opciones.explicacion: The indirect style uses subjunctive I and «dass» conjunction or investment without «wer… der».

bloques.frase: Wer nicht rechtzeitig absagt, ___ muss die Gebühr vollständig entrichten.

opciones.explicacion: The subject of the main prayer requires the demonstrative pronoun masculine in nominee «der».
«den» is accusative and the verb «muss» needs subject in nominative.
«dem» is dative and the main prayer claims active grammatical subject.

bloques.pregunta: What is the meaning of this statement?
bloques.frase: Wer anderen uneigennützig hilft, dem gebührt aufrichtiger Dank.

opciones.texto: Those who help others selflessly deserve sincere thanks.
opciones.explicacion: «gebühren» rules the right («dem gebührt Dank») to express legitimate merit.

opciones.texto: Those who receive help must pay it immediately with cash.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase praises the person who provides the uninterested aid («uneigennützig hilft»), does not impose a collection.

opciones.texto: No one who provides assistance to its neighbours is obliged to keep confidentiality.
opciones.explicacion: It is not about the duty of confidentiality but about the merit of gratitude.

bloques.frase: Wem die Leitung wichtige Projekte anvertraut, ___ schätzt man als Experten.

opciones.explicacion: In the main sentence «man» is the subject and the person evaluated acts as a direct object in accusative («den schätzt man»).
«der» would be nominating, but the subject position is already covered by «man».
«dem» is dative, while the verb «schätzen» requires direct accusative object.

bloques.pregunta: Why in the «Wer fleißig lernt, der besteht die Prüfung» sentence does the verb «lernt» go to the end and «besteht» go after «der»?

opciones.texto: Because the clause with «wer» is a subordinate (verb at the end) and the clause with «der» is the main (investment by taking position 1).
opciones.explicacion: The subordinate functions as the first orational element, so the main one begins with the correlative pronoun followed by the verb.

opciones.texto: Because both verbs must always be placed contiguous at the center of the phrase.
opciones.explicacion: The verbs are separated by the coma and the correlative pronoun «der».

opciones.texto: Because «wer» reversed the order of the main verb and «der» sent it to the infinitive.
opciones.explicacion: Neither of the two verbs goes into infinitive; both are conjugated in the present.

bloques.frase: Wer regelmäßig übt, der macht Fortschritte
bloques.explicacion: «wer» introduces the conditional subordinate and «der» heads the main clause with verb in position two.

bloques.pregunta: Select the construction with generalizer correlative that shows the exact case agreement:

opciones.texto: Wer hart arbeitet, dem stehen viele Türen offen.
opciones.explicacion: «wer» is nominative in the subordinate; in the main «stehen viele Türen offen» the beneficiary requires dative («dem»).

opciones.texto: Wer hart arbeitet, den stehen viele Türen offen.
opciones.explicacion: «den» incurs an accusative error when the expression requires a condition.

opciones.texto: Wer hart arbeitet, der stehen viele Türen offen.
opciones.explicacion: «der» is nominating or feminine and does not match the required function in the main.

intro: When we formulate general statements, proverbs, universal conditions or standards without an explicit nominal antecedent for people, German uses the correlative structure **wer …, der …** (who, that, that).
